long_biography.plain_text:
Pincus grew up in New Orleans, where his father managed hotels and restaurants. After studying architecture at the University of Virginia, he earned a master's degree from Columbia and worked at several design practices. He helped establish Bureau V, then combined a design career with a sailing school and charter company he started in 2006.

Grand Banks opened in 2014 inside a converted wooden fishing boat at Manhattan's Pier 25. Pincus handled practical design, permitting and early operations while his brother Miles brought complementary maritime experience. Their company added new dining venues in parks, marinas and restored craft across New York and New Orleans. Pincus now runs the enterprise as chief executive and continues to direct complex preservation projects on the waterfront.
